title: Hash Maps & Sets
subtitle: Trade repeated searches for a table of precisely the information a future step needs.
variables: n and m = input lengths; u = distinct keys; k = requested count/window; L = total characters; R = number of returned items. Expected hash-table bounds assume well-distributed hashes, O(1) key hash/equality and fixed-size arithmetic; collisions can make a lookup O(u) and a build O(n²). Hashing a fresh length-l string/tuple costs O(l); Python may cache string hashes but equality still can scan characters. Python integers have bit-length-dependent costs. Space distinguishes auxiliary state from output; dict preserves insertion order, set has no ordering contract.
